Inorganic Chemistry Basics

The laboratory stores machines without switching them off. Each machine includes a removable instruction note.

Each night the electrolyzer uses 10 base power and 1 L water to produce 112 g hydrogen and 888 g oxygen. Efficiency reduces power; performance increases water throughput; quality adds hydrogen without extra water. Efficiency applies at a 1:2 ratio. The separator uses 6 power per base batch to produce 222 g oxygen and 778 g nitrogen. Same-gas stacks merge. Purchased bottles contain 100 g.

The fuel power cell is low-level contraband. Every 10 g hydrogen supplies 1 energy. Smaller remainders are saved for later. With oxygen and an output container every 1 g hydrogen combines with 8 g oxygen to produce 9 mL pure water. If the container lacks space the cell still uses hydrogen for power and keeps the unused oxygen. Produced water mixes with existing liquid.
